title: Metal for Investor Relations: Run the Raise From One Current View
summary: A knowledge graph for private equity connects your firm's deals, decisions, and relationships into one structured foundation. Metal's Context Graph is built for private capital, so every new deal starts with everything your firm has already learned.
body_markdown:
### One connected view of LPs, funds, pipeline, and activity for IR and capital formation teams


Metal for Investor Relations is a connected operating view for private-capital IR and capital formation teams. It links every LP and fund to a live fundraising pipeline, connects email and meeting activity to the right relationships, and gives the whole team one current picture of the raise.


That matters because the relationship is won in the conversation, not in the admin around it. When the state of the raise lives in one place, the team spends its time on LPs instead of on reconstructing where things stand.


### Why do fundraising teams lose track of where a raise stands?


Ask three people on a fundraising team where commitments stands and you get three answers: the pipeline tracker says one thing, the CRM says another, and the real status is buried in an inbox thread. So every partner keeps a private version of the raise, and activity capture, investor requests, and DDQs eat the hours meant for LP relationships.


The gap is not effort. The context behind each LP relationship is scattered across systems that do not talk to each other.


### How Metal for Investor Relations works


Metal closes that gap and turns it into three outcomes:


1.


**One live view of the raise the whole IR team shares**
Metal connects your fundraising sources once, then keeps them current on your[firm's context layer](https://www.metal.ai/products/context-layer) . Funds, LPs, consultants, commitments, relationships, and activity resolve into one governed view. Instead of a private tracker per partner, the whole team sees how much of the target is committed and called, which funds are in market, and who the active LPs are, all from the same current context.


2.


**LP activity that stays current on its own**
Your CRM stays the system of record. Metal is the connected context and operating layer around it, so pipeline, dashboards, and prep all read from the same current picture. Email and meeting activity connects to the right LPs, funds, and people without manual entry, so the pipeline reflects what actually happened, not what someone remembered to log.


3.


**Conviction on every LP**
Your relationship history resolves into one view, so the team prioritizes re-ups and outreach from who you know and where each LP stands, not from feel or a stale record.


### Where DDQs, requests, and reporting fit


Running fundraising on connected context is what makes the repeatable work manageable. DDQs, investor requests, meeting prep, and reporting can run as reviewed[workflows](https://www.metal.ai/products/workflows) that draw from your approved source material, preserve citations, and route anything uncertain for a person to approve before it goes out. The team approves and sends instead of retyping the same answer for the tenth time. This is the same idea behind our[chat-authored dashboards](https://www.metal.ai/blog/chat-authored-dashboards-turn-deal-questions-into-live-operating-views) : the work sits on live, governed context, not a static export.


The workflows and features below are already live with a number of IR teams: diligence and DDQ automation, investor request management, fundraising, and the writeback that keeps the system current. They are not a fixed menu. Because every workflow runs on your firm's Context Graph, your team can shape the existing ones around how you actually work, or build new ones on the same connected context.

### What your IR team gets


**Can the whole team see one live view of the raise?**


Yes. Instead of a private tracker per partner, the team opens one dashboard: how much of the cap is committed and called, who the active LPs are, and how the base breaks down by type. Pipeline, performance, and LP relations sit one tab away, all updating from the same context.


**Does LP activity stay current without manual entry?**


Yes. Outlook and Exchange activity connects to the right LPs, funds, prospects, and people, and a shared IR mailbox can be visible to the organization where configured. Meetings, notes, ownership, and next actions stay current, so the pipeline reflects what actually happened rather than what someone remembered to log.


**Can we prioritize LPs from real relationship history?**


Yes. Metal resolves your relationship history into one view, so who you know, who covers them, and where each stands is one current answer. The team can prioritize re-ups and outreach from real history, with each active LP showing days in stage, last contact, and the next action to take, rather than from feel or a stale record.
